literal: Love inside lacking life-existence, in a barren land, a withered tree sprouting is like.
translation: The life of one who lacks love in their heart is like a withered tree trying to sprout in a barren desert.
modern: மனதில் அன்பு இல்லாதவருடைய வாழ்க்கை, வறண்ட பாலைநிலத்தில் காய்ந்துபோன மரம் தளிர்ப்பது போன்றதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet uses a vivid metaphor from nature to describe the futility of a life lived without love. The poet compares a person whose heart is devoid of love (அன்பகத்து இல்லா) to a completely dried-up, withered tree (வற்றல் மரம்) standing in a harsh, barren desert (வன்பாற்கண்). Just as it is impossible for such a dead tree to sprout fresh green leaves (தளிர்த்தற்று) in a waterless wasteland, it is impossible for someone without love to flourish or experience a meaningful, fruitful life. The key words 'வன்பால்' (barren land) and 'வற்றல் மரம்' (withered tree) emphasize that love is the essential life-force, without which all outward efforts at living are utterly in vain.
